context: One internal sandbox hackathon prototype assessment; supplied five Devpost criteria, equal weights, half-point increments. Internal numeric convention, not an official Devpost result.

criteria.name: Technological Implementation
reasons: Substantial functioning integration, beyond a mock-only demo: retained actual PayPal sandbox pause/resume, sponsor capture/refund, invoice payment and verified duplicate webhook records; signed receipt survived a restart; separate supplier checkout completed two approved captures.

Current rehearsal directly composes createCallService, consent gate, mock PayPal, gradeCall and buildReceipts. call.js lines 706-780 revalidate exact terms, confirm sponsor funding before refund and establish completion through same-identity reads. Six isolated cases and concurrency/injection tests exercise meaningful boundaries.

Fresh donor routing is 11/12 versus rules 6/12 but failed the zero-wrong-mutation gate. Purchase drafting failed 11/24 versus rules 14/24, and guarded negotiation does not establish AI savings. Separate exposed-case cancellation repair does not erase evaluation failure.

criteria.name: Design
reasons: Consistent restrained typography, strong action hierarchy and plain-language outcome headings. Actual desktop and phone completed states put sponsor amount, donor result and Active gift together; the phone explicitly displays Unresolved instead of a false zero/refund completion.

Native phone selector, closed conversation disclosure, focus transfer, status region and substantial targets are visible in current source. Details retain the execution record without dominating the primary relief story.

Detailed proof still requires reading long transcript/technical explanations. The lead film preserves a wide desktop layout, so embedded phone playback makes scenario descriptions and transaction detail very small.

criteria.name: Potential Impact
reasons: A concrete after-hours nonprofit need and useful mechanism: eligible donors receive hardship relief while the subscription remains active, with sponsor funding checked first. Audience statistics in the packet provide context without being represented as this product outcome.
The anonymous rehearsal allows immediate testing of bounded situations; retained sandbox payments establish feasibility of the mechanism.

No independent target-donor/nonprofit observations, saved staff time, retention uplift, willingness-to-pay or sponsor commitment are established. Gross matched funding still incurs fees, and sponsor economics and demand remain assumptions. This limits demonstrated impact without making a production launch or formal study a mandatory hackathon feature.

criteria.name: Innovation/Idea
reasons: The combination of sponsor-funded hardship relief, conversational supported-action completion, separate exact consent, claim-level evidence, signed receipts and visible unresolved outcomes is a coherent and distinctive application idea.

It goes beyond ordinary recurring-gift account management by implementing sponsor-first relief and showing what each financial statement is backed by. Existing donor management alternatives are acknowledged, so no first-ever claim is credited.

The components and conventional gift management are established. The AI contribution has some narrow semantic-routing evidence, but mixed failed gates and the deterministic price guard limit evidence that AI adds robust distinctive value across the broader donor/procurement concept.

criteria.name: Presentation
reasons: The current landing page leads with one understandable donor-relief story, immediate rehearsal and receipt actions, and one 73-second captioned film. Older demonstrations and procurement evidence are retained inside a closed optional archive.

The seven-scene captions/provenance and required film frames communicate successful relief, no-consent/no-write, changed-charge blocking, uncertainty and original/edited receipt verification. The simulation and retained actual sandbox evidence boundaries are explicit; signature integrity is distinguished from PayPal certification.

The desktop capture contains dense UI that becomes hard to read in the phone embedded player. Narration/captions help explain the mechanism, but the visual transaction detail requires expansion or the direct rehearsal/receipt route. Full movie motion and audio were not observed in this review, so no delivery-quality claim is inferred from stills.
